gold.name: Gold
gold.importParity: MCX Gold = (COMEX $/troy oz ÷ 31.1035) × 10 × USD/INR × 1.15 (import duty 15% + GST)
gold.supplyControl: No single entity controls gold supply. Top producers: China 11%, Russia 10%, Australia 10%, Canada 5%. Central banks are the dominant holders.
demandDrivers: Central bank reserve accumulation (China, Russia, India RBI buying since 2022)
Indian jewellery (25% of global demand — wedding season Oct–Feb peaks)
Gold ETFs (institutional investment flow)
Electronics and semiconductors (industrial)
Safe-haven demand during geopolitical or financial stress
priceDrivers: USD strength — gold and dollar move inversely
US real yields (10Y TIPS) — higher real rates raise opportunity cost of holding gold
Central bank buying — especially EM central banks diversifying away from USD
Geopolitical risk — war, sanctions, banking crises lift gold
India import duty — government can change duty; each 1% duty change shifts MCX price ~₹1,000/10g
Indian rupee — a weaker INR amplifies MCX gold price even when COMEX is flat
gold.keyRisk: MCX-COMEX spread can widen when Indian import duty changes or USD/INR moves sharply — watch basis risk.
gold.taxNote: Gold ETF LTCG: 12.5% after 12 months (Budget 2024). Physical gold LTCG: 12.5% without indexation after 2 years. MCX futures gains: taxed as business income or STCG at slab rate. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

silver.name: Silver
silver.supplyControl: Top producers: Mexico 22%, Peru 14%, China 13%, Russia 7%. Unlike gold, 70% of silver supply comes as a by-product of mining other metals (copper, zinc, lead) — supply is inelastic.
demandDrivers: Industrial use (60% of demand) — solar panels, EVs, electronics, 5G
Jewellery and silverware (India is world's largest silver importer for this)
Investment demand — silver ETFs, bars and coins
Green energy transition — each solar panel uses ~20g of silver; global solar buildout is a structural demand tailwind
priceDrivers: Gold-silver ratio — historically 60–80x; when ratio spikes above 80, silver is cheap relative to gold
Industrial cycle — silver tracks copper in risk-on/risk-off regimes more than gold does
Solar capacity additions — China solar policy directly affects silver industrial demand
USD strength (inverse)
India import duty and monsoon (agri income → silver buying in rural India)
silver.keyRisk: Silver is far more volatile than gold — easily swings 3–5% in a session. High lot value (₹30L per lot) amplifies P&L. Silver Mini (5 kg) is available for smaller capital.
silver.taxNote: Same as gold futures — gains taxed as business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

crude.name: Crude Oil
crude.importParity: MCX Crude = WTI ($/bbl) × USD/INR × 1.02 (includes import duty differential)
crude.supplyControl: OPEC+ (13 OPEC members + Russia + 9 allies) controls ~40% of global oil supply and sets production quotas quarterly. Saudi Arabia is the swing producer — can flood or restrict supply unilaterally within limits. US shale (Permian Basin) is the marginal supplier that caps upside.
demandDrivers: Transportation — aviation, shipping, road fuel (60% of global oil demand)
Petrochemicals — plastics, fertilisers
Chinese industrial activity — China alone is 15% of global demand
Indian fuel demand — India is world's 3rd largest oil consumer
Seasonal driving demand (US summer, India winter)
priceDrivers: OPEC+ production decisions — each 1 mbpd cut historically lifts WTI $5–10/bbl
US EIA weekly inventory data (Wednesday 8 PM IST) — draw = bullish, build = bearish
US shale rig count (Baker Hughes, Friday) — higher rigs = more future supply = price cap
China PMI and import data — weak China demand is the biggest bearish driver
Middle East geopolitics — Strait of Hormuz tension (20% of global oil transits through it)
USD strength — oil is priced in dollars; strong USD = lower oil for non-US buyers
Seasonal: US driving season (Memorial Day–Labor Day) lifts gasoline/crude
crude.keyRisk: Crude is the most geopolitically sensitive commodity. Weekend OPEC+ surprises and Middle East flare-ups cause gap opens on Monday. Retail traders should avoid holding large overnight positions before OPEC+ meetings.
crude.taxNote: MCX crude futures gains: business income or STCG. CTT 0.01% on sell. Petrol/diesel prices in India are state-controlled and do not move with MCX crude in real time.

copper.name: Copper
copper.supplyControl: Chile (25%) and Peru (11%) together control 36% of global mined copper supply. Congo (DRC) is rising fast. The Democratic Republic of Congo + Zambia control 70% of global cobalt (copper by-product). China controls 40% of global copper smelting/refining capacity — a chokepoint even when mines are elsewhere.
demandDrivers: China construction and infrastructure (accounts for ~55% of global copper demand)
Electric vehicles — each EV uses 83kg of copper vs 22kg in ICE cars
Power grid buildout — renewable energy and grid upgrades are copper-intensive
AI data centres — each hyperscale data centre uses thousands of tonnes of copper wiring
Indian infrastructure (roads, rail, power) — growing demand centre
priceDrivers: China economic data — PMI, property sector health, stimulus announcements
LME warehouse stock levels — low inventory signals supply tightness
Mine supply disruptions — strikes in Chile/Peru (frequent), floods, political instability
AI and energy transition narrative — long-term structural demand story
USD strength (inverse — copper priced in dollars on LME/COMEX)
COMEX-LME basis — arbitrage between US and London markets creates price signals
copper.keyRisk: Copper's large lot size (2,500 kg, ~₹24L contract value) makes it high-capital. LME price is the global benchmark; COMEX is the US proxy. MCX follows COMEX with import duty overlay. Copper is called 'Dr. Copper' because it has the best track record of predicting global economic direction.
copper.taxNote: MCX copper futures: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

natgas.name: Natural Gas
natgas.importParity: MCX NatGas = Henry Hub ($/mmBtu) × USD/INR. Indian LNG import prices track JCC (Japan Crude Cocktail) and long-term contracts — not Henry Hub directly.
natgas.supplyControl: Russia was Europe's dominant gas supplier (pre-2022); now LNG from US, Qatar, Australia fills the gap. The US is the world's largest natural gas producer. Qatar controls ~25% of global LNG trade. Russia's Gazprom still controls the pipelines to much of Eastern Europe. Australia is Asia's largest LNG exporter.
demandDrivers: Power generation — natural gas is the marginal fuel for electricity in the US and increasingly India
Winter heating demand (Northern Hemisphere — Nov–Feb is the peak demand season)
Industrial feedstock — fertiliser production (gas is the key input for urea)
LNG exports from US — high US export demand tightens domestic supply
AI data centre power — gas-fired power plants are being restarted in the US to power AI data centres
priceDrivers: US weather forecasts (3–7 day) — cold snaps drive heating demand and spike prices overnight
EIA Weekly Storage Report (Thursday, 8 PM IST) — draw vs injection vs 5-year average
Hurricane season (June–November) — Gulf of Mexico production disruptions
European LNG import demand — post-Russia sanctions, Europe competes with Asia for LNG cargoes
Henry Hub (US benchmark) — MCX NatGas follows Henry Hub via import parity
AI data centre electricity demand — structural new demand source from 2024 onward
natgas.keyRisk: Natural gas is the most volatile commodity on MCX — daily moves of 5–10% are common. Prices swing on a single weather forecast update. Low margin (₹20–30K) amplifies leverage massively relative to capital. MCX NatGas tracks Henry Hub, not Indian city gas prices.
natgas.taxNote: MCX NatGas futures: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.
